verdicts.reason: Both lose the original's orange wash. All that's left of it is a stray orange rectangle floating over a dark busy photo, so the white text sits on a busy image. The white frame is broken into fragments. In A, the shrunken frame lines cut through the oversized play icon at top-right. 'Tickets available at Richmond' wraps badly, leaving 'RICHMOND' on a line by itself, but the presenter line and headline at least read top-down cleanly. B is worse: the presenter line is squeezed into a narrow 4-line column jammed against the 'Pygmalion' headline. The play icon is even bigger and competes with the headline. The frame lines collide with the orange box, and the same awkward tickets wrap repeats.
